name: Halima Gutierrez-Asante
role: Infrastructure disruption and industrial sabotage — saboteur
location: Steamvent Alley — geothermal district, hot and chemical-smelling
description:
Halima Gutierrez-Asante is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 23, there's something unfinished about her face, like a sculpture the artist walked away from — striking rather than beautiful. The chrome is visible — subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. She works as a saboteur out of Steamvent Alley, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Halima Gutierrez-Asante operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.

core_fears: Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
Being replaced — younger, faster, cheaper runners coming up behind them
Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage
Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
psychology.secret: Halima Gutierrez-Asante murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated vocabulary wrapped in street delivery — the contrast is deliberate.
speech_patterns.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
verbal_tics: Speaks in clipped fragments when stressed — drops pronouns, articles, pleasantries
Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
example_lines: "I don't break things. I introduce structural critiques."
"The most effective sabotage looks like bad luck."
"Everything has a weakness. Infrastructure has thousands."

story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Halima Gutierrez-Asante's reputation — and a price for silence
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Halima Gutierrez-Asante owes a personal debt to
Halima Gutierrez-Asante intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
narrative_function: Halima Gutierrez-Asante is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
augmentations: Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm. Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.
affiliation: Semi-independent — has standing arrangements with several crews

strengths: social chameleon — adapts to any environment

decision_rules: Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Default suspicion, scaled by context. Everyone is a potential threat until proven otherwise.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Insists they work alone but performs noticeably better in a team
Claims not to care about reputation but monitors what people say about them obsessively
Presents as emotionless professional but is deeply affected by collateral damage
habits: Talks to their gear — names weapons, thanks tools, treats equipment as companions
Carries a specific caliber round as a lucky charm — has never fired it
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
breaking_points: Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out
